gaps.sentence: She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: ___ she was utterly exhausted, she stayed to help clear up.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a known fact: she was exhausted and still stayed.

gaps.sentence: He talks ___ he owned the place.
gaps.explanation: 'As if/though + past' describes behaviour contrary to fact (he doesn't own it).

gaps.sentence: She has decided to cycle to work ___ taking the bus.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + -ing' = in place of the bus journey.

gaps.sentence: ___ did he apologise, but he also refunded the full amount.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only did he..., but he also...' is the correlative pattern with inversion.

gaps.sentence: ___ you finish early, come and give us a hand.
gaps.explanation: 'If' introduces a real condition; 'in case' would change the meaning to precaution.

gaps.sentence: ___ a staffing shortage, the clinic closed early.
gaps.explanation: 'Due to + noun phrase' states the cause in formal register.

gaps.sentence: ___ had I closed my eyes than the alarm went off.
gaps.explanation: The 'than' in the sentence forces 'No sooner', the only linker paired with than.
